newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-FRENCHMAN TROUSSIER NAMED NIGERIA MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCHMAN TROUSSIER NAMED NIGERIA MANAGER.

text.p: Frenchman Phillipe Troussier, former coach of the Ivory Coast national side, was named as Nigeria's new soccer manager on Thursday.
Announcing the appointment, Abdulmumini Aminu, chairman of the Nigeria Football Association (NFA), said Troussier would earn a monthly salary of $10,000.
The length of the contract and other personal details would be announced later, he said.
Amodu Shaibu, who had taken over the team on a temporary basis after Dutchman Jo Bonfrere quit last October, was sacked last month for "gross misconduct" and "insubordination".
Bonfrere had quit the job alleging poor treatment and interference in his duties by the sports authorities.

Troussier, nicknamed "White Wizard", is currently trainer of Moroccan first division side FUS Rabat. He has also trained division one teams Kaizer Chiefs and ASEC Mimosas in South Africa and Ivory Coast respectively.
He was Ivory Coast coach in 1993 but lost the job after the country failed to qualify for the 1994 World Cup from the group from which Nigeria qualified.
"Troussier is now saddled with the responsibility of ensuring Nigeria qualify for the 1998 World Cup finals in France," Aminu said.
Nigeria are second behind Guinea in a World Cup group of four teams from which one will qualify. The Olympic champions are at home to Guinea in their next qualifier on April 5.
